title: How is task usage measured in Zapier? (updated 5 November 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A task is any successful action; triggers, filters, paths, formatter, delay and storage steps use no tasks in Classic Zaps; Zapier MCP uses 2 tasks per successful call; from 1 December 2026 each completed Next Gen Zap run uses at least 1 task.

title: How Zap triggers work (updated 29 May 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Most triggers poll; instant triggers use webhooks; polling interval Free 15 minutes, Professional 2 minutes, Team and Enterprise 1 minute.

title: Decide how your Zap handles errors with advanced settings (updated 29 May 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Autoreplay retries failed steps and is an account-wide setting on Professional plans and higher; Zapier pauses a Zap that errors on 95% or more of its runs in the last 7 days unless overridden.

title: Set up custom error handling (updated 10 April 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Error handlers run an alternative path when a step errors; available on Professional, Team and Enterprise; Zapier sends no error notification email when an error handler runs.

title: Using Code by Zapier (updated 13 July 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. JavaScript (Node.js 22) and Python 3.13 only; standard run time 1 second Free, 30 seconds Professional and Team, 2 minutes Enterprise; 512 MB memory; Code by Zapier does not support storing secrets in code; use an API by Zapier connection.

title: Trigger Zaps from webhooks (updated 29 May 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Webhooks by Zapier on Professional, Team and Enterprise, not Free; payload limit 10 MB (2 MB for Catch Raw Hook); active hooks always return 200; the unique URL is the only access control described.

title: Request approval to keep your workflow running with Human in the Loop (updated 26 October 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Request Approval pauses a Zap run for a reviewer to approve, decline or edit; timeout and reminder options; Professional, Team and Enterprise; cannot be inside or after a Looping step.

title: Zapier MCP: your first MCP workflow
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Zapier auto-provisions a server with actions pre-enabled for connected apps; an agent can find and enable new actions during a request; two tasks per successful call; never share a connection token.

title: Introducing credits: new billing unit live in Make
supports: Opened with WebFetch (page created 5 Aug 2025; a companion page gives 27 Aug 2025 as the effective date). Credits replaced operations, converted 1:1; by default 1 operation equals 1 credit; some AI modules use more.

title: Error handlers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Five error handlers: Skip, Retry (stores incomplete executions), Resume, Commit, Rollback (only for modules that support transactions).

title: Fix errors and warnings
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Runs stop after 45 minutes (10 minutes on Free); without a Retry handler no automatic retries except built-in handling of connection and rate-limit errors; an error in the trigger deactivates the scenario.

title: n8n Community License FAQ (Sustainable Use License)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Self-hosted n8n may be used for internal business purposes; building workflows for clients on your own instance is allowed if clients cannot create or edit them; hosting n8n as a service where others build workflows is not.

title: n8n plans and pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. An execution is a single run of the entire workflow, whatever the number of steps; cloud plan names Starter, Pro, Business and Enterprise.

title: Handle errors gracefully
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Each workflow can set an error workflow that runs when an execution fails and must start with the Error Trigger node; the Stop and Error node forces an execution to fail.

title: Human-in-the-loop for AI tool calls
supports: Opened with WebFetch. An AI Agent pauses before calling a tool that needs review; the reviewer sees the tool and parameters; approve runs it, deny cancels it; channels include n8n Chat, Slack, Teams and Gmail.

title: Limits of automated, scheduled, and instant flows
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 29 Oct 2026). 500 actions per workflow; run duration 30 days including pending approvals; run retention 30 days; minimum recurrence 60 seconds; continuously failing flows turned off after 14 days.

title: Types of Power Automate licenses
supports: Opened with WebFetch (dated 22 Sep 2026). Power Automate Free is included with work or school accounts and limited to standard connectors; Premium adds premium and custom connectors; Process licences for flows and unattended bots.

title: Manage data policies
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 14 Aug 2026). Connectors sorted into Business, Non-business and Blocked groups; connectors in different groups cannot share data; blocked connectors cannot be used; admin roles needed to create policies.

title: Get started with Power Automate approvals
supports: Opened with WebFetch (updated 29 Oct 2026). Approval types including everyone must approve, first to respond and sequential; approvals connector is standard; responses from Outlook, Teams or the action center.

title: Getting started with Airtable automations
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Monthly run limits: Free 100, Team 25,000, Business 100,000, Enterprise Scale 500,000; failed and successful runs count; failure notifications go to the last user who turned the automation on.

title: Database automations
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Available on paid plans; Free plans can create Slack notification automations only; triggers and actions including send mail and send webhook; database automations cannot be triggered by other automations.

title: Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Verify signatures with the raw body; return 2xx quickly; live-mode retries for up to three days; endpoints may receive the same event more than once, so log processed event IDs; order not guaranteed.

title: Deliver webhooks through HTTPS
supports: Opened with WebFetch. HMAC verification with X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256; one-second connection and five-second total timeout; 8 retries over 4 hours; Admin API subscriptions deleted after 8 consecutive failures; dedupe with X-Shopify-Webhook-Id.

title: Eliminating Toil (Site Reliability Engineering, chapter 5)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Toil is manual, repetitive, automatable, tactical work with no enduring value that grows with the service; Google aims to keep toil below 50% of each SRE's time.

title: Toyota Production System
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Jidoka, automation with a human touch: machines stop when an abnormality occurs and the andon board alerts workers, so people need not watch machines.

title: SEC Charges Knight Capital With Violations of Market Access Rule (press release 2013-222, 16 October 2013)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Old unused code left in the router; incorrect deployment in late July 2012; on 1 August 2012 more than 4 million orders in 45 minutes and a loss of more than $460 million; 97 automated warning emails not acted on; inadequate deployment controls and incident procedures.

title: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Requirements including honest headers and subject lines, a physical postal address and an opt-out honoured within 10 business days; no exception for business-to-business email; penalties up to $53,088 per email.

title: Data (Use and Access) Act factsheet: UK GDPR and DPA (27 June 2025)
publisher: GOV.UK, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Section 80 replaces UK GDPR Article 22 with Articles 22A to 22D, a more permissive framework for solely automated decisions with safeguards (information, representations and challenge, human intervention); the Act comes into force in stages.

title: Data (Use and Access) Act factsheet: PEC Regulations (27 June 2025)
publisher: GOV.UK, Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The soft opt-in is extended to charities, so they can send marketing emails and texts to people who have shown interest in their work without explicit consent, with an opt-out.

title: AI Act: regulatory framework for AI (last updated 19 October 2026)
publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
supports: Opened with WebFetch. People should be made aware when they interact with a machine such as a chatbot; transparency rules take effect in August 2026; the AI Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026 and moved high-risk dates to 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028.
